title: High-Spending Customers by Product
statement: The schema has `customers`, `products`, and `orders` (each order references one customer and one product, with a quantity). Write a query joining all three tables to return `name` and `total_spent` (SUM(quantity * price)) per customer, for customers whose total spend is greater than 500, ordered by total_spent descending.
starter_code:
SELECT c.name, SUM(o.quantity * p.price) AS total_spent
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON -- TODO
JOIN products p ON -- TODO
GROUP BY -- TODO
HAVING -- TODO
ORDER BY total_spent DESC;
hints: Join orders to customers on customer_id = id, and orders to products on product_id = id
GROUP BY the customer name, then filter the aggregated total with HAVING (not WHERE, since it's a filter on the SUM)
Chitra spends exactly 500, which is not strictly greater than 500 - she should be excluded
